essence: Thirteen members named: the whole Śākta doctrine held in one breath.
Rest, transformation, return: thirteen members, nothing outside.
Supreme wisdom revealed by Śambhu himself across every Trika treatise.
The bulb's site measured: five below the navel, two above — the wheel's station.
Breath held, mind cast there, winds mastered into the middle — that is entry.
Entry sealed by custom; the form shown: horned-pond wheel, six spokes, firm.
Pomegranate-red bulb, third member — form as contemplation itself.
Mind steadied in the middle, obstruction gone — then the mark is given.
The unstruck digit mid-wheel, line-bound, serpent-coiled — the sign.
Her abiding spans high and low, sun and moon, thousand-sun bright.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta with vīra-utsāha (wonder braced by resolve)
rasa.justification: Wonder at the body revealed as doctrine — measured bulb, red wheel, serpent-coiled digit, thousand-sun radiance; the optative prescriptions (cast, lead, place, point out) summon the practitioner's resolve inside the wonder.

sections.BOUNDARY: No piercing happens here, no trembling, no rest. The ladder, the signs, and the repose belong to members pledged but not yet paid.
sections.EXPLANATION: The thirteen divide into naming and enacting: vv1-3 count the members whole, vv4-10 walk the first five in the body. Sthāna is found by measure, praveśa by breath-restraint and mind cast exactly, rūpa by teacher-shown vision (a firm six-spoked wheel), lakṣa by steadied mind meeting handled wind, lakṣaṇa by gazing at the serpent-coiled unstruck digit. Vijñāna here means the esoteric doctrine itself (sdv), and śākta carries its Kaula weight.
sections.FUNCTION: Lays measurable ground for the ascent and seals it with revealed authority, so every later tremor and rest already owns its place in a counted whole.
sections.KEY TERMS: sthāna (standing place) — the kanda found by finger-measure; praveśa (entry) — breath restrained, mind cast, wind led middle-ward; rūpa (form) — the seen wheel, consisting of contemplation (cintanātmaka); lakṣa (mark) — the assigned focus, distinct from the sign; lakṣaṇa (sign) — the observed unstruck digit; kanda (bulb) — pomegranate-red, six-spoked station; vijñāna (esoteric doctrine) — supreme thirteenfold knowledge.
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: All thirteen members pledged at the opening govern the whole work; raising through return, enacted beyond, are already owed by the list.
sections.RELATED: Trika treatises as the doctrine's carriers (v3); śākta as kaula (sdv) — the Kuṇḍalinī frame present though the name never sounds; Mahānaya thirteenfold table as the ready gloss bank.
sections.SUMMARY: Thirteen members hold the Śākta wisdom entire, from the bulb's measured site to the thousand-sun radiance of the Goddess. Breath restrained and mind fixed, entry opens; a six-spoked wheel appears, pomegranate-red; the unstruck digit coils serpent-like at the wheel's heart. Naming becomes seeing: the counted doctrine already glows in the body.
